result.stdout:
dt-docs: build and check a project docs site.

Usage:
  dt-docs init [<dir>] [options]    Create a project docs repo
  dt-docs dev [options]             Serve the site locally, reloading as you edit
  dt-docs check [--format <f>]      Check docs.json, MANIFEST.md and rule IDs
  dt-docs build [--format <f>]      Check, then build the site into build/, sign-in included
  dt-docs serve [options]           Serve the last build, with search
  dt-docs new <kind> <page>         Create a page from a page template
  dt-docs guide [<topic>]           Print the writing guide for a kind of page
  dt-docs --version                 Print the tool's version

Run every command but init in the repo, or below it: the tool finds docs.json above the current
directory. Options after dev and serve go to Docusaurus unchanged, for example --port 3001.

init takes --name, --description, --sections, --ci, --repo-url, --branch and --tenant-id, and asks
for any it isn't given. --sections is a comma-separated list of folders, each with an optional label:
domain,systems=Acme Systems,features. --ci is github, azure or none.

new takes a kind (domain, systems, feature, adr or page) and the page's path under docs/ without its
extension: dt-docs new domain returns writes docs/domain/returns.md.

--format is text, github or azure. It defaults to github on GitHub Actions, azure on Azure
Pipelines and text anywhere else. check and build exit 1 on any finding.
